title: Your First Weekend at Butler University, Shared as Cards
description: A conservative, under-21-safe sequence using evergreen campus destinations and recurring new-student behaviors.

cards.title: 1. Start at Admission’s Landmark
cards.subtitle: Orient yourself at Robertson Hall
cards.notes: Use Robertson Hall as a named reference point, then open the official campus map before moving onward.
cards.short_summary: A clear first waypoint on Butler’s mapped campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler’s official campus map identifies Robertson Hall as the Office of Admission.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor wayfinding is generally available; office entry depends on posted business hours.

cards.title: 2. Learn the Union Layout
cards.subtitle: Find student services and meeting spaces
cards.notes: Locate Student Involvement, the Dean of Students, dining, lounges, and organization offices before exploring farther.
cards.short_summary: A practical orientation stop inside Butler’s student union.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler lists Atherton Union’s student offices, organization spaces, meeting rooms, dining, and bookstore.
cards.access_notes: Building and individual office hours vary; some rooms may be reserved.

cards.title: 3. Test Your Library Route
cards.subtitle: Walk from Atherton to Irwin
cards.notes: Find the Information Commons desk, public computers, study tables, printers, and room-reservation information.
cards.short_summary: A reconnaissance visit to Butler’s main academic library.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler documents Irwin’s study seating, Information Commons, computers, wireless access, and print services.
cards.access_notes: Check weekend library hours; reservable study rooms are limited to current Butler students.

cards.title: 4. Take the Garden Loop
cards.subtitle: Free public paths since 1928
cards.notes: Walk established paths, identify the pond and carillon, and avoid garden beds or spaces reserved for events.
cards.short_summary: A low-pressure outdoor loop through Butler’s public gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler states that Holcomb Gardens is free and open to the public and serves as student gathering space.
cards.access_notes: Free public outdoor access; specific areas may be reserved for events.

cards.title: 5. See Hinkle from the Outside
cards.subtitle: Historic athletics landmark
cards.notes: Circle only public exterior paths unless you hold a ticket or are attending an officially open program.
cards.short_summary: A first look at Butler’s historic fieldhouse without assuming event access.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler identifies Hinkle Fieldhouse as a 1928 campus arena hosting basketball, volleyball, and other events.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is distinct from venue entry; events may require tickets and security screening.

cards.title: 6. Learn the Blue Lineage
cards.subtitle: East of Hinkle Fieldhouse
cards.notes: Read the memorial plaques and compare the bronze Blue II sculpture with the limestone bulldog at Atherton.
cards.short_summary: A compact lesson in Butler’s live-mascot history.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler says the memorial honors official and unofficial live mascots and features a bronze sculpture modeled on Blue II.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial; approach respectfully and yield to ceremonies or maintenance.

cards.title: 7. Activate Your 24/7 Study Option
cards.subtitle: Levinson Family Hall, second floor
cards.notes: Bring your Butler ID, locate the card reader and study areas, and review the quiet-space expectation.
cards.short_summary: A first check of Butler’s round-the-clock student study floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler states that the Science Library provides 24/7 ID-card access, study spaces, rooms, whiteboards, and computers.
cards.access_notes: 24/7 access is limited to Butler students, faculty, and staff with ID cards.

cards.title: 8. Find the Blue House
cards.subtitle: Across from Schrott Center
cards.notes: Mark the center on your mental map and check its calendar for reflection, dialogue, or community programs.
cards.short_summary: A wayfinding stop for Butler’s meaning-making communities.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler’s orientation materials locate the Compass Center in the blue house across from Schrott Center.
cards.access_notes: Program and building hours vary; respect audience-specific gatherings.

cards.title: 9. Check the Night Sky Schedule
cards.subtitle: North end of campus
cards.notes: Consult the public-program schedule and separate free telescope viewing from the paid planetarium presentation.
cards.short_summary: An evening astronomy stop with a clearly defined free component.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler offers public observatory tours and states that telescope viewing is always free when weather permits.
cards.access_notes: Viewing depends on scheduled public access and weather; the telescope dome requires stairs.

cards.title: 10. End in ResCo’s 24/7 Seating
cards.subtitle: Residential College
cards.notes: Use the seating area only if your residence access permits, keep noise appropriate, and clean the table afterward.
cards.short_summary: A late indoor landing place documented as continuously available to students.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler states that the Midtown Provisions seating area is available to students 24/7.
cards.source_title: Midtown Provisions Opens a New Chapter in Butler Dining
cards.access_notes: Student seating is described as 24/7; residence-building entry may require authorized card access.
